filed_hypothesis: Batch filtering may prioritize section flags over explicit function declarations.
captain_refutation: decompile_all.rs resolve_targets builds the list from prog.function_entries_executable(); section executability, not the declaration, decides it.
decisions: THE HYPOTHESIS HOLDS, but the filter lives one crate below where the captain pointed. `resolve_targets` (kuna-cli/src/decompile_all.rs:1269) only calls `ConsoleProgram::function_entries_executable` (kuna-console/src/engine.rs), and that is where the section-CODE test is. Fixing it in the engine rather than in the CLI is what makes `decompile-project`, the wasm whole-binary walk and `decompile_graph` honour a declaration too -- all four surfaces derive their target list from that one function.

MEASURED CAUSE: every section of the witness is 0xc0000040 (INITIALIZED_DATA|READ|WRITE) -- .text as much as .NEOpack -- so no entry passes `flags & section_flags::CODE != 0` and the list is empty for the whole image, not just for the declared address. Without the declaration discovery finds 6 import pointer slots and no bodies; with it, `kuna functions` reports 7 and `kuna decompile <bin> entry` emits `void entry(void) { sub_4f7990(); }`. Nothing in the decompiler refuses the address; only the batch target list does.

A NEW `declared_entries` SET, NOT `declared_extents`. Reusing the extent map would have honoured `--define-function 0x4f7001-0x4f700c` and silently dropped the bare `--define-function 0x4f7001`, which asserts exactly the same thing about entry-ness and just leaves the extent natural. `declare_function` writes both, so the console `function bounds` surface gets the same behaviour for free.

NO OPTION, per AGENTS.md and the tooling-track brief: a whole-binary run that drops a function the caller declared and that `kuna decompile` decompiles is wrong output, not a judgement call, and this cannot change emitted C for any binary that passes no declaration. The sweep confirms it: 123 in-repo fixture binaries, 2,973 functions, zero changed bodies.

THE RESIDUAL IS THE OTHER HALF OF THE TITLE. With the target list fixed, a bare `decompile-all` on the same image still answered `count: 0`, exit 0, error null -- the arm `zero_discovery_error` deliberately takes when the image carries no executable content. That test read section flags and program headers only, which a packer defeats for free by not setting the bit. `classify_code_evidence` now also accepts an entry point that lands inside a section as evidence of code, and the message names the address and the section and points at `--define-function`. A resource-only PE keeps its honest empty answer because `object` reports its entry as the bare image base, which no section covers.

THE FOLDED SIBLING `batch-decompilation-succeeds-bodies` IS CLOSED BY THE RESIDUAL, not contradicted by it. Its acceptance wanted `decompile-all <BIN> --json` (no declaration) to exit non-zero; it now does, with a message naming 0x4f7001. The two acceptances only looked opposed because they were read as the same command -- one passes --define-function and one does not.

THE ACCEPTANCE'S TARGET IS A DATASET BINARY, so --promote refuses it. tests/cli/batch-silently-omits-explicitly.json keeps the acceptance clause (`count > 0`) verbatim against a 1,536-byte PE32 written byte by byte by pe_datasection_entry_i386.py: two sections both flagged 0xc0000040, AddressOfEntryPoint at an odd offset inside the second, and an 11-byte entry that calls into the first. It reproduces the witness exactly -- `count: 0, error: null` on the unpatched tree, `void entry(void) { sub_401000(); }` after. The sibling probe batch-silently-omits-explicitly-diagnosis.json pins the residual on the same fixture.
sweep_method: pre/post `kuna decompile-all --json` over every in-repo fixture binary (stdout and exit code compared byte for byte; the old binary is the main tree's build at the base commit)
sweep_changed_detail: the only differing binary in 123 is the new fixture pe_datasection_entry_i386.exe itself, which moves from `count: 0, error: null, exit 0` to `count: 0` with the entry-point diagnosis and exit 1. No emitted C changed anywhere, and no pre-existing binary changed its exit code.
speed_method: no measurement taken: the added work is one BTreeSet lookup per canonical entry (empty set, so a single compare) and, only on a run that already discovered nothing, one extra section walk
parity: make test PARITY OK 675/675; make test-stages PARITY OK 677/677; make test-cli 75/75; make check-spec OK; kuna catalog --check OK; make rust-test green except the two known environment artifacts recorded below
gate_notes: make rust-test reported two failures, neither from this change. (1) kuna-cli docs_cli::embedded_docs_match_the_files_on_disk: docs/cli.md was edited while the suite was compiling; re-run alone it passes 23/23. (2) kuna-decomp verify_w10_proto_unlock::w10_proto_unlock_const_return_collapses_no_tied_roundtrip: the repipe launcher exports KUNA_DECOMP_TEST at the worktree's own decomp_test_dbg, so the C++ oracle is kuna and its `unsigned int` reads as drift from the pinned `xunknown4`; `env -u KUNA_DECOMP_TEST cargo test -p kuna-decomp --test verify_w10_proto_unlock` is 4/4 green.
